card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill calculated by one method may differ from that by another. Who may specifically decide the method to be used?
card.back: Goodwill calculated by one method may differ from the goodwill calculated by another method. Hence, the method by which goodwill is to be calculated, may be specifically decided between the existing partners and the incoming partner.
card.quote: Goodwill calculated by one method may differ from the goodwill calculated by another method. Hence, the method by which goodwill is to be calculated, may be specifically decided between the existing partners and the incoming partner.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is ____ at the time of admission of a partner.
card.back: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.
card.quote: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill appearing in the books will be ____ by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their ____.
card.back: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.
card.quote: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill by capitalisation of average profits: how is it ascertained?
card.back: Under this method, the value of goodwill is ascertained by deducting the actual firm's capital in the business from the capitalized value of the average profits on the basis of normal rate of return.
card.quote: Under this method, the value of goodwill is ascertained by deducting the actual firm's capital in the business from the capitalized value of the average profits on the basis of normal rate of return.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill premium credited to old partners is retained in business: what additional entry is passed?
card.back: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.
card.quote: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Define goodwill in terms of the reputation of a firm.
card.back: Goodwill is the value of the reputation of a firm in respect of the profits expected in future over and above the normal profits.
card.quote: Goodwill is the value of the reputation of a firm in respect of the profits expected in future over and above the normal profits.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Formula: Goodwill by capitalisation of average profits.
card.back: Goodwill = Capitalised value − Net Assets
card.quote: Goodwill = Capitalised value − Net Assets

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Formula: Goodwill by capitalisation of super profits.
card.back: Goodwill = Super Profits × 100 / Normal Rate of Return
card.quote: Goodwill = Super Profits × 100 Normal Rate of Return

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: What is goodwill?
card.back: Over a period of time, a well-established business develops an advantage of good name, reputation and wide business connections. This helps the business to earn more profits as compared to a newly set up business. In accounting, the monetary value of such advantage is known as "goodwill".
card.quote: Over a period of time, a well-established business develops an advantage of good name, reputation and wide business connections. This helps the business to earn more profits as compared to a newly set up business. In accounting, the monetary value of such advantage is known as "goodwill".

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Define goodwill in simple words.
card.back: In simple words, goodwill can be defined as "the present value of a firm's anticipated excess earnings" or as "the capitalised value attached to the differential profit capacity of a business".
card.quote: In simple words, goodwill can be defined as "the present value of a firm's anticipated excess earnings" or as "the capitalised value attached to the differential profit capacity of a business".

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Name the 5 main factors affecting the value of goodwill.
card.back:
1. Nature of business: A firm that produces high value added products or having a stable demand is able to earn more profits and therefore has more goodwill.
2. Location: If the business is centrally located or is at a place having heavy customer traffic, the goodwill tends to be high.
3. Efficiency of management: A well-managed concern usually enjoys the advantage of high productivity and cost efficiency.
4. Market situation: The monopoly condition or limited competition enables the concern to earn high profits which leads to higher value of goodwill.
5. Special advantages
card.quote: The main factors affecting the value of goodwill are as follows: 1. Nature of business: A firm that produces high value added products or having a stable demand is able to earn more profits and therefore has more goodwill. 2. Location: If the business is centrally located or is at a place having heavy customer traffic, the goodwill tends to be high. 3. Efficiency of management: A well-managed concern usually enjoys the advantage of high productivity and cost efficiency. This leads to higher profits and so the value of goodwill will also be high. 4. Market situation: The monopoly condition or limited competition enables the concern to earn high profits which leads to higher value of goodwill. 5. Special advantages: The firm that enjoys special advantages like import licences, low rate and assured supply of electricity, long-term contracts for supply of materials, well-known collaborators, patents, trademarks, etc. enjoy higher value of goodwill.

source.section: 2.5.2 Factors Affecting the Value of Goodwill

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: In a partnership firm, name the circumstances in which valuation of goodwill may be needed.
card.quote: Normally, the need for valuation of goodwill arises at the time of sale of a business. But, in the context of a partnership firm it may also arise in the following circumstances: 1. Change in the profit sharing ratio amongst the existing partners; 2. Admission of new partner; 3. Retirement of a partner; 4. Death of a partner; and 5. Dissolution of a firm involving sale of business as a going concern. 6. Amalgamation of partnership firms.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Since goodwill is an ____ it is very difficult to accurately calculate its value.
card.back: Since goodwill is an intangible asset it is very difficult to accurately calculate its value.
card.quote: Since goodwill is an intangible asset it is very difficult to accurately calculate its value.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Name the important methods of valuation of goodwill.
card.back:
1. Average Profits Method
2. Super Profits Method
3. Capitalisation Method
card.quote: The important methods of valuation of goodwill are as follows: 1. Average Profits Method 2. Super Profits Method 3. Capitalisation Method

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Average profits method: how is goodwill valued?
card.back: Under this method, the goodwill is valued at agreed number of 'years' purchase of the average profits of the past few years.
card.quote: Under this method, the goodwill is valued at agreed number of 'years' purchase of the average profits of the past few years.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Average profits method: how should goodwill be calculated from the past average profits?
card.back: The goodwill, therefore, should be calculated by multiplying the past average profits by the number of years during which the anticipated profits are expected to accrue.
card.quote: The goodwill, therefore, should be calculated by multiplying the past average profits by the number of years during which the anticipated profits are expected to accrue.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Past average profits Rs. 20,000, likely to continue for another three years: goodwill by average profits method?
card.back: the value of goodwill will be Rs. 60,000 (Rs. 20,000 × 3)
card.quote: if the past average profits of a business works out at Rs. 20,000 and it is expected that such profits are likely to continue for another three years, the value of goodwill will be Rs. 60,000 (Rs. 20,000 × 3),

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Super profits method: on what basis is it desirable to value goodwill?
card.back: Therefore, it is desirable to value, goodwill on the basis of the excess profits and not the actual profits.
card.quote: But it is contended that the buyer's real benefit does not lie in total profits; it is limited to such amounts of profits which are in excess of the normal return on capital employed in similar business. Therefore, it is desirable to value, goodwill on the basis of the excess profits and not the actual profits.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Firms capital includes partners capital and ____ but excludes ____ and goodwill.
card.back: Firms capital includes partners capital and reserves and surplus but excludes fictitious assets and goodwill.
card.quote: Firms capital includes partners capital and reserves and surplus but excludes fictitious assets and goodwill.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The goodwill under the super profit method is ascertained by ____ the super profits by certain number of years' purchase.
card.back: The goodwill under the super profit method is ascertained by multiplying the super profits by certain number of years' purchase.
card.quote: The goodwill under the super profit method is ascertained by multiplying the super profits by certain number of years' purchase.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Super profits Rs. 3,000, benefit likely to last 5 years: goodwill by the super profits method?
card.back: the goodwill will be valued at Rs. 15,000 (3,000 × 5)
card.quote: If, in the above example, it is expected that the benefit of super profits is likely to be available for 5 years in future, the goodwill will be valued at Rs. 15,000 (3,000 × 5).

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Steps in the super profits method of valuing goodwill, in order.
card.back:
1. Calculate the average profit,
2. Calculate the normal profit on the firm's capital on the basis of the normal rate of return,
3. Calculate the super profits by deducting normal profit from the average profits, and
4. Calculate goodwill by multiplying the super profits by the given number of years' purchase.
card.quote: Thus, the steps involved under the method are: 1. Calculate the average profit, 2. Calculate the normal profit on the firm's capital on the basis of the normal rate of return, 3. Calculate the super profits by deducting normal profit from the average profits, and 4. Calculate goodwill by multiplying the super profits by the given number of years' purchase.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: In how many ways can goodwill be calculated under the capitalisation method? Name them.
card.back:
(a) by capitalizing the average profits, or
(b) by capitalising the super profits.
card.quote: Under this method the goodwill can be calculated in two ways: (a) by capitalizing the average profits, or (b) by capitalising the super profits.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Steps in valuing goodwill by capitalisation of average profits, in order.
card.back:
1. Ascertain the average profits based on the past few years' performance.
2. Capitalize the average profits on the basis of the normal rate of return to ascertain the capitalised value of average profits
3. Ascertain the actual firm's capital (net assets) by deducting outside liabilities from the total assets
4. Compute the value of goodwill by deducting net assets from the capitalised value of average profits
card.quote: (i) Ascertain the average profits based on the past few years' performance. (ii) Capitalize the average profits on the basis of the normal rate of return to ascertain the capitalised value of average profits as follows: Average Profits × 100/Normal Rate of Return (iii) Ascertain the actual firm's capital (net assets) by deducting outside liabilities from the total assets (excluding goodwill and ficticious assets). Firms' Capital = Total Assets (excluding goodwill) – Outside Liabilities Where outside Liabilities include both long term and short term Liabilities. (iv) Compute the value of goodwill by deducting net assets from the capitalised value of average profits, i.e. (ii) – (iii).

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Steps in valuing goodwill by capitalisation of super profits, in order.
card.back:
1. Calculate capital of the firm
2. Calculate normal profits on capital employed
3. Calculate average profit for past years, as specified
4. Calculate super profits by deducting normal profits from average profits
5. Multiply the super profits by the required rate of return multiplier
card.quote: (i) Calculate capital of the firm, which is equal to total assets (excluding goodwill and ficticious assets) minus outside liabilities. (ii) Calculate normal profits on capital employed. (iii) Calculate average profit for past years, as specified. (ii) Calculate super profits by deducting normal profits from average profits. (iii) Multiply the super profits by the required rate of return multiplier, that is,
card.note: Capital of the firm = total assets (excluding goodwill and fictitious assets) minus outside liabilities.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Under the capitalisation of super profits method, goodwill is what?
card.back: In other words, goodwill is the capitalised value of super profits.
card.quote: In other words, goodwill is the capitalised value of super profits.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The amount of goodwill worked out by this method will be ____ as calculated by capitalising the average profits.
card.back: The amount of goodwill worked out by this method will be exactly the same as calculated by capitalising the average profits.
card.quote: The amount of goodwill worked out by this method will be exactly the same as calculated by capitalising the average profits.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Under AS 26, how is internally generated goodwill treated?
card.back: Internally generated goodwill should not be recognised as an asset.
card.quote: Internally generated goodwill should not be recognised as an asset.

source.section: Applicability of Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Hidden goodwill: how is the value of goodwill found when it is not given?
card.back: Sometimes the value of goodwill is not given at the time of admission of a new partner. In such a situation it has to be inferred from the arrangement of the capital and profit sharing ratio.
card.quote: Sometimes the value of goodwill is not given at the time of admission of a new partner. In such a situation it has to be inferred from the arrangement of the capital and profit sharing ratio.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: A and B, equal partners with capitals of Rs. 45,000 each, admit C for 1/3 share; C brings Rs. 60,000. Find the goodwill.
card.back: Hence, it can be inferred that the difference is on account of goodwill i.e., Rs. 30,000 (Rs. 1,80,000 − Rs. 1,50,000).
card.quote: Hence, it can be inferred that the difference is on account of goodwill i.e., Rs. 30,000 (Rs. 1,80,000 − Rs. 1,50,000).

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: In the hidden goodwill example (goodwill Rs. 30,000, C's share one-third), how is C's share treated?
card.back: In this, C's Current account will be debited by Rs. 10,000 (his share of goodwill) and A and B's Capital accounts credited by Rs. 5,000 each.
card.quote: In this, C's Current account will be debited by Rs. 10,000 (his share of goodwill) and A and B's Capital accounts credited by Rs. 5,000 each.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: On the admission of a new partner, to whom does the goodwill of the firm belong?
card.back: On the admission of a new partner the goodwill of the firm belongs to the old partners.
card.quote: On the admission of a new partner the goodwill of the firm belongs to the old partners.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Why must goodwill adjustments be made in the old partners' capital accounts on admission?
card.back: some adjustments must be made into the capital accounts of the old partners for goodwill so that the new partner will not acquire a share in that profit which the firm earns because of its goodwill earned before admission without making any payment for the same.
card.quote: It means that on the admission of a new partner some adjustments must be made into the capital accounts of the old partners for goodwill so that the new partner will not acquire a share in that profit which the firm earns because of its goodwill earned before admission without making any payment for the same.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: What is the new partner's share of goodwill (premium for goodwill)?
card.back: As stated earlier, the incoming partner who acquires his share in the profits of the firm from the existing partners brings in additional amount to compensate them for loss of their share in super profits. It is termed as his share of goodwill (also called premium for goodwill).
card.quote: As stated earlier, the incoming partner who acquires his share in the profits of the firm from the existing partners brings in additional amount to compensate them for loss of their share in super profits. It is termed as his share of goodwill (also called premium for goodwill).
